borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
decision_conditions: The proposal fails to provide clear and consistent plans regarding No.65. The block plan (drawing ref: DRGNO00193, dated 10/08/2025) inaccurately depicts No.65 as wider than adjoining dwellings despite the proposed demolition of the side extension, and the site boundary is unclear between No.65 and No.65a. The proposal could prejudice third parties who may otherwise have wished to comment on the application; the proposed development cannot be accurately assessed and it cannot be demonstrated that it would be supported by the Development Plan.  As such, the proposal is contrary to:National Planning Policy Framework National Planning Policy Framework (MHCLG, December 2024)Policy D4 of the London Plan (March 2021);Policies SP2 and DMD1 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September, 2024)

The proposed development fails to provide the units with separate private external amenity space, presenting a poor quality of accommodation and as such would be contrary to:National Planning Policy Framework (MHCLG, December 2024)Policy D6 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policy DMD1 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September, 2024)

The proposed dwelling, by reason of its siting, scale and design, would represent an incongruous form of development that disrupts the established pattern and undermines the distinctive banjo cul‑de‑sac character of the Becontree Estate. The detached building fails to reflect the prevailing built form and would result in the loss of openness on a prominent corner plot, with poor design quality, weak street presence and an unsympathetic roof form. The proposal is therefore considered to be harmful to the historic character of area and contrary to:National Planning Policy Framework (MHCLG, December, 2024)Policies D4 and HC1 of the London Plan (March 2021) Policies SPP6, SP2, DMD1 and DMD4 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September, 2024)

The proposed development fails to demonstrate that additional demand for parking from the development could be adequately accommodated in the surrounding area. The proposal is therefore likely to add unacceptably to parking stress and congestion in the vicinity of the application site.  As such, it fails to comply with the following policies which seek to ensure proposals show how car parking will be designed and managed and to take into consideration on-street parking availability and existing and planned public transport provision:National Planning Policy Framework (MHCLG, December 2024)Policies T1, T2, T3, T4, T6 and T6.1 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policies SP8, DMT1 and DMT2 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September 2024)

The proposal fails to demonstrate compliance with statutory BNG requirements. The application lacks consistency and does not provide sufficient, reliable evidence to confirm that the statutory 10% BNG would be achieved, nor that impacts on existing habitats and green space have been appropriately assessed or mitigated. This is contrary to:Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990

The scale, siting and design of the proposed development would result in a harmful loss of outlook and daylight to neighbouring occupiers. It would create a sense of enclosure and have an overbearing impact, thereby constituting unneighbourly development. The proposal is therefore contrary to:

- National Planning Policy Framework  (MHCLG, December 2024)

- Policy D4 of the London Plan (March 2021);

- Policies SP2 and DMD1 of the Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan (September 2024)
